key_insight: The paper makes RUDEs more stable and interpretable by combining logarithmic input compression, split neural networks, and a differentiable thermodynamic constraint, enabling multi-mode constitutive models that generalize better to unseen flows.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path to data-driven rheology models that can be deployed in CFD and used to predict processing behavior of complex soft materials more reliably.
method: Log-compress rheological invariants to improve training conditioning.
Use a split-network mmRUDE architecture to reduce stiffness and improve mode-wise learning.
Apply a differentiable projection layer to enforce the Clausius--Duhem inequality at each time step.
evidence_signal: The framework was trained on LAOS data and validated on synthetic multi-mode Giesekus and experimental silicone melt cases, where it remained stable and accurate for unseen steady shear, stress growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The added constraints and architecture improve robustness, but deployment still depends on careful implementation and sufficient training coverage across the relevant flow regimes.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
